quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 20 Questions • Passing Score 15

questions.question: What is the best way to brake in a straight line?

options.text: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
Use both brakes while locking the rear wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes without locking either wheel.
questions.explanation: On a straight road, you can stop fastest by using both brakes together. Avoid locking either brake.

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing a brightly-colored helmet?

options.text: It helps other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: A brightly-colored helmet is recommended. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers notice you on the road.

questions.question: Which action does NOT help a rider stay visible?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: Stay visible by wearing bright clothing with reflective materials, using your headlight always, and using your turn signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcycles ride through a curve?
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is normally best, groups should switch to single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering and leaving highways.

questions.question: What does it mean when a rider's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn right.
questions.explanation: Hand signals show turns or stops when mechanical signals are not used. A left arm bent at the elbow and pointing upward means the rider will turn right or change lanes to the right.

questions.question: When should you leave more space between you and other vehicles?

options.text: When it is colder than usual.
When you are following other motorcycles.

questions.explanation: A two-second following distance is normally enough. Use more space when roads are wet or icy, as your bike needs more distance to stop.

questions.question: How should a group of riders merge onto a highway?
questions.explanation: Although staggered formation works best normally, groups should use single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering and leaving highways.

questions.question: Which item is NOT important for avoiding serious injury?
questions.explanation: Wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots that cover your ankles, and durable gloves to protect yourself.

questions.question: What should you do to help drivers merging from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Move to another lane if possible.
Do nothing since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging may not see your motorcycle. Give them space by moving to a different lane when you can.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane before passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front.
Without signaling so you don't distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing on the left. Signal your intention, check for traffic, pass safely, then signal and return to your lane.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can your body eliminate per hour?
questions.explanation: Your body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time it takes to lower your blood alcohol content (BAC) varies. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Why is riding next to another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may have a hard time reaching a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It stops other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The driver could turn into your lane without warning. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake in non-emergency situations.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Why should you check your motorcycle before riding?

options.text: Only a mechanic can find problems.
You should not check it before riding.
You should check it only after riding.
It helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you find mechanical problems or broken equipment.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. This helps you spot problems that could be dangerous.

questions.question: Why should riders not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Motorcycle mirrors are smaller and show less.
Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
Mirrors take your eyes off the road and should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like cars. You cannot rely only on mirrors to see what is behind you. Check over your shoulder regularly as part of your riding routine.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Long rides in cold weather can cause all of these except:
questions.explanation: Long cold-weather rides can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from the cold.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever?
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your controls are before you start riding.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs more space to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle brake light is small and not as noticeable as car brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers see it, especially when you slow down faster than they expect.
